## LitAnatomy v0.2.0

Papers from their PDFs, more ways to look papers up, screening for systematic reviews, and synthesis notes for a whole collection.

### Adding papers
- **From PDFs:** drop PDFs, or a folder of them, on the drop area on Home or anywhere in the window. You can also paste files copied in your file manager (Ctrl+V), click the drop area, or use Add papers › From PDFs…. LitAnatomy reads each PDF's properties and first pages, finds its DOI, arXiv ID or ISBN, looks it up, and checks that the title it finds is the one on the PDF. The PDF stays linked, so Open PDF works straight away. A PDF without an identifier is searched for on Crossref by its title; failing that, it is added with the details the PDF itself gives, marked for you to check. The preview says how each paper was found.
- **By arXiv ID, ISBN or PubMed ID,** as well as by DOI: paste `arXiv:2301.12345`, an arxiv.org link, `ISBN 978-…`, `PMID: 31452104` or a PubMed link, one or many at once. A preprint that has since been published gets the journal's details and keeps its arXiv ID.
- **Fill in** on the Metadata tab now also works from a paper's arXiv ID or ISBN when it has no DOI.
- Dropping one PDF on an open paper still links it to that paper.

### Systematic reviews
- **Screening:** in a collection's settings, turn on "Screen these papers" and write its inclusion and exclusion criteria (IC1, IC2…, EC1, EC2…).
- Each paper in the collection gets a **Screening** tab with its abstract: include it, exclude it or mark it "maybe", tick the criteria that apply and add a note. Ticking an exclusion criterion excludes the paper. **Next paper to screen** takes you straight to the next one.
- The collection's list shows how far the screening has got, how many papers were excluded for each criterion, and a Screening column. Click a count to show only those papers, or select several papers and set their decision at once.
- **PRISMA counts:** copy the numbers for a PRISMA flow diagram in one click.
- Excluded papers stay in the collection, so the counts add up. The synthesis matrix can show the screening as a column.

### Synthesis
- Each collection has a **Synthesis** page (next to Matrix): group its papers into **themes**, note what each theme's papers share and how each paper fits, and keep overview notes on patterns across the papers. Papers not in any theme yet are listed, so none is forgotten.
- **Draft a related-work outline** from the themes: a section per theme listing its papers with their `\cite` keys and contributions, then the open problems from the papers' Research Gaps notes. Edit it freely, then export it as Markdown or LaTeX.
- A paper shows the themes it belongs to.

### Keyboard shortcuts
- **Tab** and **Shift+Tab** move between a paper's notes, in reading order.
- **Ctrl+Enter** (Cmd+Enter on a Mac) stops editing a field; a filled-in note then shows formatted. In the Add by identifier dialog it looks the papers up.
- **Esc** leaves a field, then goes back a level: from a paper to its collection, from a collection to Home.
- **Ctrl+Shift+Delete** on an open paper (with no field selected) asks to move it to the Trash.
- **F1**, or the new keyboard button at the bottom left, lists every shortcut.

### Smaller changes
- Home's "Add a paper" area is more compact, with a drop area for PDFs and folders that lights up while you drag files over the window.
- The papers under "Continue where you left off" and the collection cards on Home can be clicked anywhere, and no longer select their text instead.
- **Linux (Wayland):** dropping files didn't work, because the windowing library LitAnatomy uses doesn't support it on native Wayland windows yet. LitAnatomy now runs through XWayland, where dropping works. Settings › PDFs can switch back to a native Wayland window.

### Library format
Libraries opened by v0.2.0 are upgraded and can no longer be opened by v0.1. Make a backup first (Settings › Library file › Back up…) if you might go back.
